**China’s Shenzhou-23 Crew Recovers Biological Samples from Tiangong Space Station**
China’s Shenzhou-23 astronauts have retrieved biological samples from the external experiment platform of the Tiangong space station’s Mengtian laboratory module, concluding the fourth round of a space exposure experiment that began in June 2023. According to Global Times, the recovered materials, which include nanozymes, actinomycetes, and plant seeds, were exposed to the vacuum, high-energy particle radiation, and extreme temperature fluctuations of space for approximately five months. The samples are scheduled to return to Earth aboard the Shenzhou-23 spacecraft for laboratory analysis to assess their radiation damage and biological tolerance. While the results do not yet confirm the survival of the organisms, researchers aim to use the data to develop radiation-resistant treatments and biological support systems for future lunar missions, where astronauts lack Earth’s protective magnetic field and atmosphere. Currently in their sixth month aboard the station, the Shenzhou-23 crew—Zhu Yangzhu, Zhang Zhiyuan, and Li Jiaying—continues to conduct research on microgravity’s effects on the human body and station maintenance.

**DF Police Recover Rare Gold Coins and Melted Gold in Operation Against 'Wig Thief'**
On the morning of November 16, 2026, the 2nd District Police Station (2ª DP) in Asa Norte, Brasília, executed search warrants at two jewelry shops in Taguatinga and Sol Nascente/Pôr do Sol, recovering rare gold coins and melted gold nuggets. According to Deputy Chief of Police Diego Costa, the items were found during an operation to recover stolen goods from the apartment of former district deputy Cristiano Araújo (MDB). The recovered items, which include a 2000 Banco Central do Brasil 500th Anniversary gold coin (valued at up to R$ 7,500) and a corresponding silver coin (valued at approximately R$ 1,500), are part of a total seizure estimated to exceed R$ 1 million. 

The investigation links the recovery to Bruno da Silva Ribeiro, known as the 'wig thief,' who was arrested for the November 8 burglary of Araújo’s high-end apartment in SQN 303. Costa stated that Ribeiro had sold the stolen jewelry to the targeted shops, and police suspect the melted gold fragments are derived from melted-down stolen items to obscure their origin. While the police have not yet confirmed that all recovered items belong to Araújo, they noted that several high-value items, including luxury handbags and watches, remain missing. 

Ribeiro, who was also arrested in March 2026 for a series of burglaries in the Sudoeste neighborhood causing over R$ 500,000 in damages, is described as having an ostentatious lifestyle funded by illicit activities, including international travel and VIP events. He typically used the 'fake broker' ruse and a female wig to bypass building security. The police are now calling on other victims to provide information to link the recovered items to their original owners.

**Nigerian Navy Dismantles Illegal Refining Sites in Rivers State, Recovers 56,800 Litres of Crude**
The Nigerian Navy dismantled two illegal crude oil refining sites in Rivers State on November 13, 2026, recovering a total of 56,800 litres of suspected stolen oil, according to a statement by Director of Naval Information Captain Abiodun Folorunsho. The operation, conducted under Operation DELTA SENTINEL by personnel from NNS SOROH, targeted the Olodo and Okarki locations in the Ogbogolo axis of Ahoada West Local Government Area. The Navy described the action as part of a sustained effort to disrupt crude oil theft networks and protect national economic security.

**Army recovers 1957 bomber radio from Alaska glacier after 69 years**
Soldiers from the U.S. Army's 59th Signal Battalion recovered a BC-348-Q radio from the wreck of a TB-29 bomber on Bomber Glacier in Alaska on August 10, 2026. The 311th Signal Command announced the recovery on November 14, 2026, a day before the 69th anniversary of the 1957 crash. The radio, which the bomber's crew used to send their final distress call, had been buried in the ice since November 15, 1957. The original crash killed six of the ten men aboard the aircraft, which was returning from a training mission to Elmendorf Air Force Base. The site is located behind a 6,000-foot rock wall in a remote Alaskan wilderness area. Captain Steven Sparks, who commands the 59th Signal Battalion's Headquarters Detachment, discovered the radio in a hiker's video in early 2026. After securing approvals from various state agencies, a nine-person team led by Sparks hiked and climbed to the site, descending a 2,000-foot vertical drop to find the radio 200 feet from the fuselage. The team transported the radio back to base camp on August 10, and on August 11, a UH-60L Black Hawk helicopter from the 207th Aviation Regiment of the Alaska Army National Guard airlifted the soldiers and the radio to Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson. The Army has not disclosed where the radio will be stored or if it will be restored.

A total of 32 people were transported to hospitals, including two police officers who fell into the river; no injuries were reported as critical, and eight individuals remained hospitalized as of Saturday. A passenger described the cargo ship sounding its horn repeatedly before the impact, after which the cruise ship's crew gathered passengers to distribute life jackets before the vessel rolled over. The Port Authority has filed a lawsuit claiming the incident caused at least $1 million in damages to its facilities. A judge issued an order allowing federal authorities to temporarily take control of the cargo ship, which has since been moved from the collision site. The U.S. Coast Guard stated the cargo ship appeared to lose steering capability, though the exact cause remains undetermined. The National Transportation Safety Board is expected to release a preliminary report within 30 days.

**NNRA Convenes Emergency Meeting Over Theft of Radioactive Sources in Rivers State**
The Nigerian Nuclear Regulatory Authority (NNRA) convened an emergency meeting of the National Nuclear Security Committee (NNSC) on Monday at its headquarters in Abuja following a reported theft of radioactive sources and security breach at an industrial radiography facility in Rivers State. According to the NNRA, the incident involved unauthorized access to the facility's storage pit, resulting in the theft of six source projectors—two of which contained Ir-192 radioactive sources—and one transit container. The operating company formally reported the incident to the NNRA, which subsequently notified the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) through its Incident and Trafficking Database (ITDB), the Unified System for Information Exchange in Incidents and Emergencies (USIE), and the Agency's Incident and Emergency Centre. The NNRA stated these reports were made in compliance with the Convention on Early Notification of a Nuclear Accident and the Convention on Assistance in the Case of a Nuclear Accident or Radiological Emergency. During the meeting, national security agencies and stakeholders assessed the safety and security implications of the breach. The Committee agreed on modalities for investigating the incident and recovering the missing equipment, assigned specific responsibilities to participating agencies, and outlined measures to mitigate potential risks, reaffirming the NNRA's commitment to safeguarding radioactive sources through regulatory oversight and international collaboration.

**Alert issued in seven Mexican states after radioactive medical materials stolen following vehicle rollover**
Mexican federal authorities have activated a preventive alert in seven states—Tlaxcala, Puebla, Hidalgo, Morelos, Veracruz, Estado de México, and Mexico City—following the theft of nine boxes containing radioactive material on November 7, 2026. The incident occurred after a cargo vehicle belonging to the National Institute of Nuclear Research (ININ) overturned on the Huamantla-Tlaxcala highway while transporting the material from La Marquesa in Estado de México to Xalapa, Veracruz. 

The stolen cargo includes three Technetium-99m generators (with activities of 200, 650, and 1,000 millicuries), four boxes of Iodine-131 (400 millicuries each), one box of Thallium (12,000 millicuries), and one box of Samarium (100,000 millicuries). The National Civil Protection Agency (CNPC) and the National Commission for Nuclear Safety and Safeguards (CNSNS) warn that while the materials are classified as Category 4 (low risk) by the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), direct contact or manipulation of the containers—especially if opened or damaged—could pose health hazards. Authorities have confirmed there is no radioactive leakage from the overturned vehicle, but the condition of the stolen packages remains unknown.

The article contextualizes the incident with a history of radioactive thefts in Mexico, including a December 2013 heist of a Cobalt-60 source (Category 1, high risk) in Hidalgo, which was recovered two days later after being removed from its shielding. It also cites a series of Iridium-192 thefts between 2017 and 2021, most of which were recovered. The CNSNS and Ministry of Health have also documented cases of lost sources and radioactive materials found in scrapyards and industrial facilities, including Radio-226 in 2022. Authorities urge the public not to touch or move any suspicious containers and to report findings to 911.

**Stolen Radioactive Actinium-225 Recovered in São Paulo**
On October 6, 2026, the National Nuclear Security Authority (ANSN) announced that the São Paulo State Civil Police recovered radioactive material containing Actinium-225 (Ac-225) that had been lost after the transport vehicle was stolen. The material was located on the evening of Monday, October 5, 2026, in an empty lot in the Zona Leste district of São Paulo. According to the ANSN, the shielding characteristics matched the missing volume, and the content remained intact. The ANSN stated that the material, which corresponds to a small quantity intended for injectable therapeutic use in cancer patients, poses 'low radiological risk to the population' due to the small amount involved, the short-range nature of the alpha particles emitted by Ac-225, and the fact that the packaging was found whole. The material remains under police custody and will undergo necessary technical verification before being moved to a secure area for evaluation.

On October 5, 2026, the São Paulo Civil Police located a container holding Actinium-225, a radioactive isotope valued at R$ 30,000, in an abandoned lot in the São Rafael neighborhood of the Zona Leste (East Zone) of São Paulo. The material, originally stolen from a van on Rodovia Presidente Dutra on Thursday, October 1, 2026, was intended for cancer treatment at Hospital A.C.Camargo. The Autoridade Nacional de Segurança Nuclear (ANSN) confirmed the container, manufactured in the United States, had not been breached and posed a low contamination risk in its current state, though it warned against opening it. The van itself was recovered on Saturday, October 3, in Ferraz de Vasconcelos, but was found dismantled and missing the cargo. **Radioactive Medical Cargo Stolen in São Paulo; Driver Held Hostage**

The incident was reported to the 2nd Police District of Guarulhos. According to the São Paulo Public Security Secretariat (SSP), four criminals—two in a car and two on a motorcycle—approached the 58-year-old driver around 22:00. The driver was held hostage until the morning of Friday, October 2, when he was released near Avenida Marechal Tito in the Itaim Paulista district of São Paulo. The Autoridade Nacional de Segurança Nuclear (ANSN) is investigating the case. While the full vehicle and cargo have not been recovered, tracking systems led authorities to find parts of the van in a dismantling yard. **Stolen Radioactive Device Recovered in Temuco After Seven Months**
A nuclear densimeter, a radioactive device stolen in February 2026 from a truck at kilometer 476 in Cabrero, Bío Bío region, was recovered during an operation in Temuco, La Araucanía region, on Monday night, September 21, 2026, according to BioBioChile. The emergency began when a passenger using the inDrive app left the device in the vehicle and fled after arriving at the Rodoviario, claiming the item was worth a lot of money. The driver alerted Carabineros, triggering a security protocol at the Labocar station, which isolated the police facility and closed vehicular and pedestrian traffic. A municipal school located next to the station preemptively suspended its classes to facilitate the safe removal of the equipment. The device had been missing for seven months since the theft. Following expert assessments, procedures to return the device to its owner company have been initiated.

**DPS Recovers 100-Millicurie Cesium-137 Source in Midland County**
The Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS), in coordination with local, state, and federal partners, recovered a sealed cesium-137 radioactive source in Midland County over the weekend of July 24-25, 2026. A corporal from the DPS Radiological/Nuclear Threat Detection Unit detected elevated radiation levels on Friday, July 24, during a routine patrol near South County Road 1210. Subsequent surveys confirmed a 100-millicurie cesium-137 source, manufactured in April 1967, located approximately 6 to 8 inches below the surface. On Saturday, DPS personnel, alongside the FBI, Texas Department of State Health Services, Midland Fire Department Hazardous Materials Team, Midland Health Department, Midland Emergency Management, and Chevron security, executed a recovery operation involving radiological assessments and excavation. Officials established hot and cold zones, monitored radiation continuously, and rotated personnel to limit exposure. The source was safely recovered without injuries, contamination, or public threat. According to DPS, the operation demonstrated the unit's capabilities, which include one lieutenant, one sergeant, and six corporals equipped with vehicle-mounted systems, backpack detectors, and unmanned aircraft, alongside a statewide initiative to equip all state troopers with personal radiation detectors.

**U.S. on the brink of losing measles elimination status as outbreaks surge in Guatemala and Mexico**
The United States is on the verge of losing its status as a country that eliminated measles in 2000, according to a committee of independent experts convened by the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO). Citing anonymous sources, several U.S. media outlets reported that the committee determined the U.S. no longer meets the required conditions, a claim the U.S. Department of Health did not immediately confirm to AFP. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the U.S. has recorded 5,182 confirmed cases since the beginning of 2026, surpassing the 2,289 cases recorded in all of 2025 and marking the highest level since 1991. 

While the U.S. outbreak has drawn global attention, PAHA data updated on November 5 indicates the situation is more critical in Latin America. Guatemala has reported 34,748 cases and 53 deaths, a dramatic reversal from just nine cases in 2025, with a significant proportion of cases occurring in young adults aged 20 to 29. In Mexico, 13,761 infections and 50 deaths have been recorded; however, the epidemic is currently declining from a peak of 1,215 daily active cases to approximately 16, according to Mexican Health Secretary David Kershenobich. The outbreaks in both countries were driven by imported cases from the U.S. and a drop in vaccination rates that occurred during the COVID-19 pandemic. 

Experts note that measles is extremely contagious and requires at least 95% vaccination coverage for containment. In 2025, only 92.4% of U.S. preschool children were vaccinated, with lower local rates, partly due to a surge in religious and philosophical exemptions since the pandemic. Krutika Kuppalli, an infectious disease doctor in Texas, described the erosion of these protections as 'deeply frustrating.' PAHO is scheduled to hold a press conference on Tuesday to address the U.S. decision and the ongoing outbreaks in Guatemala and Mexico.

The CDC has confirmed six measles-related deaths, with Pennsylvania reporting 1,542 cases. **Pennsylvania and Wisconsin Report Measles Deaths as US Cases Surpass 5,000**
On Friday, November 13, 2026, health officials in Pennsylvania and Wisconsin each reported a measles-associated death, marking the seventh and second deaths respectively in their states during the current outbreak. According to the Pennsylvania state health department, the latest death involved an unvaccinated resident of Montour County; the state has recorded 1,542 cases across 46 counties, including 305 hospitalizations.
